items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: His name was J.C. Higginbottom... We rehearsed at Higgy's sister's house at times... Higginbottom was ahead of the rest of us as far as style was concerned... he had been inspired by someone. All that I can say is that Higgy could blow better than anyone else in the orchestra.

ctx.x: I was still rehearsing with Edgar Courance, Alex, a pianist named Trotter, a drummer named Bill Johnson. John Coleman eventually came to Cincinnati and rehearsed with us also. The group was now composed of trumpet, clarinet, alto sax, C melody sax, piano and drums. We had no job in sight but we were amateurs and enjoyed the music we were playing. Trotter, the pianist, was a professional musician who had been put down by most of the other professionals because he was an alcoholic. He played some fine piano as far…

Sometime later, an amateur trombone player came to Cincinnati and he stayed rehearsing with us. His name was J.C. Higginbottom and it was at his sister's house that Dyer and Dolly Jones used to have their sessions when I lived on Hathaway Street. His siter was now living on Kenyon Avenue, very near the house of Clarence Page. We rehearsed at Higgy's sister's house at times, but
most of them were at Alex's house on Court Street.
